examples.knowledge_point: Dividing an Imaginary Number by a Complex Number
examples.problem: If $z_1=3\textrm{i}$ and $z_2 = 2+5\textrm{i},$ then what is $z_1$ divided by $z_2?$

feedback.worked_solution:
The denominator is $1-\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1+\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1+\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-3-4\text{i}}{1-\text{i}} & =\frac{-3-4\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1+\text{i}}{1+\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-3-3\text{i}-4\text{i}-4{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-3-7\text{i}-4(-1)}{1-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-3-7\text{i}+4}{1+1} \\  & =\frac{1-7\text{i}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{1-7\text{i}}{2}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{7}{2}\text{i}
$$
